guideTitle: 6 Best Power Failure Night Lights in 2026
metaTitle: Best Power Failure Night Lights in 2026
metaDescription: Six power failure night lights compared: plug-in lights that glow at dusk, brighten when the power cuts out, and double as a flashlight for late-night walks.
introParagraphs: A power failure night light does two jobs with one plug. On an ordinary evening it behaves like any other night light, glowing softly in a hallway or bathroom so you can see where you are stepping. When the power cuts out, a built-in battery takes over, and the same light becomes your emergency light, often with a handle or fold-out design so you can lift it off the wall and carry it. For anyone who gets up in the night, that two-in-one design is the most natural backup there is.

The six picks here share that idea but differ in the details. The GE 2 Pack and the Energizer 4 in 1 add dusk to dawn sensors and spell out their lumen levels, the Camelion and Infinity X1 sets use motion sensing, the Wennyn combines motion and dusk sensing, and the ROSSEX 4 in 1 is a straightforward plug-in light with a rechargeable lithium battery. Each approach has strengths, which we explain pick by pick and in the comparison sections.

We evaluated these lights from their listing specs and typical buyer feedback, so brightness and timing figures are the makers' claims. The aim is practical: lights that are easy to place, gentle at night and dependable when needed, with enough detail to match each product to the room it will guard.

products.name: GE Plug in Power Failure Night Light, 2 Pack
products.description:
The GE 2 Pack is the best all-around pick because it spells out what each mode does. According to the listing, each light works as a 40 lumen portable flashlight, a 40 lumen emergency light, a 5 lumen night light and a 5 lumen tabletop light. A dusk to dawn sensor turns the light on when the room gets dark and off when daylight returns, so nobody has to touch it.

That clarity makes the lights easy to live with. A 5 lumen night glow is gentle enough for a bedroom hallway, while the 40 lumen emergency level is bright enough to see a room and its obstacles. The lights switch to battery power automatically during an outage, which is exactly the behavior you want from a plug-in backup.

Two units are enough for a small home or for the two critical spots, usually the bedroom and the bathroom, but they will not cover a larger house. Compared with the Energizer 4 in 1, the GE gives the clearest published lumen figures. Compared with the Camelion, it relies on a light sensor instead of motion, which many people find more predictable. Set the pair in outlets at about knee height so the light falls across the floor. Both lights also work as 40 lumen flashlights, so in a long outage you can carry one and leave the other glowing in the hallway. Avoid plugging it behind a curtain or a sofa where the sensor cannot see.
products.bestFor: Bedroom and bathroom paths where a gentle glow and clear published output matter.
pros: Published lumen levels for every mode
Dusk to dawn sensor works hands-free
cons: Only two units in the pack
No motion sensing for hands-free brightening

products.name: Energizer 4-in-1 Power Failure Night Light
specs: Auto on and off light sensor
Power failure, night, tabletop and flashlight modes
products.description:
The Energizer 4 in 1 combines the four functions its name promises: power failure light, night light, tabletop light and portable flashlight. An automatic light sensor turns it on in low light and off when the room brightens, and the emergency mode activates when household power is lost. It is the kind of device you plug in once and forget about until it is needed.

It appeals mostly through simplicity and familiarity. There is no motion setting to adjust, no color mode to learn and no companion app, so it is an easy gift for a relative who dislikes gadgets. The listing does not publish lumen figures for each mode, so we do not state any here.

Compared with the GE 2 Pack, the Energizer offers the same basic concept but in a single unit and with fewer published details, so it is a better fit when you want one light and trust the brand. Keep it in the room where you are most likely to be moving at night, and lift it out occasionally to confirm that it still lights for several minutes on its battery. With no published lumen figure, run it beside a GE for one night to judge which hallway glow you prefer, and remember that one Energizer covers a single spot where the Camelion pack covers three.
products.bestFor: People who want one simple, familiar light with no extras to learn.
pros: Light sensor handles on and off
cons: Single unit does not cover several rooms

products.name: Camelion 4-in-1 Power Failure Night Light, 3 Pack
products.description:
The Camelion set brings motion activation to the category. During an outage, the listing says, the built-in rechargeable battery keeps the night light ready, and it serves as a night light and power failure light while plugged in. You remove it from the outlet, fold it and use it as a flashlight.

The motion sensor suits late-night walks: the light comes on when you step into the hallway and goes off after you leave. That saves battery during an outage and avoids glowing all night. The cost is a bit more unpredictability, since the light may react to a pet or a passerby.

Three units cover the bedroom, bathroom and stairs, and the listing stresses that no disposable batteries are required. Compared with the Infinity X1, the Camelion is simpler, with fewer color options. Compared with the ROSSEX, it adds motion sensing. It is a solid pick for households that want a light that turns on only when someone is nearby. Make sure children and pets cannot trigger it all night in a room where someone is sleeping. If the light fires too often, move it to a spot that faces the corridor rather than the bed.
products.bestFor: Hallways where a light that only glows when you walk past saves battery.
cons: May react to pets and passersby
Fold-out design has a learning step

products.name: Infinity X1 Power Failure Rechargeable Night Lights, 3 Pack
products.description:
The Infinity X1 is the most configurable light here. Each unit offers three selectable color temperatures: 3000K warm, 4500K neutral and 6000K cool white. The motion sensor detects movement within a range of 3 to 5 meters, and the lights activate automatically during a power outage. The listing also mentions an emergency USB-C output.

The warm 3000K setting is a real plus at night, because it is easier on the eyes than a cool white glow. The motion range means the light starts early enough to guide you before you reach the stairs. The USB-C output gives you a small bonus in an outage, though you should not expect it to replace a proper power bank.

All that flexibility means more to set up than the GE or Energizer. Set the color once and leave it. Compared with the Camelion, the Infinity X1 offers more control and a longer sensing range, so it is the better pick for a longer hall or a larger room. Its 3 to 5 meter motion range reaches further than the GE's dusk to dawn sensor, which only reacts to darkness. The warm setting is generally the best match for bedrooms, while the cool one suits a utility area.
products.bestFor: Longer hallways and anyone who wants a warm glow at night.
pros: Three color temperatures to choose from
cons: USB-C output is a minor extra

products.name: Wennyn 4-in-1 LED Night Light Emergency Backup
specs: Motion and dusk to dawn sensing
products.description:
The Wennyn pairs two sensors. According to the listing, it senses dusk to dawn and also motion: the light turns on at night in a dimmed state and goes off in the day, and brightens when it detects movement. It combines night light, power outage light, flashlight and regular light functions, powered by a built-in rechargeable battery that charges when plugged in.

That combination is clever for a bedroom or bathroom. The dim glow lets you see the room, and the brighter motion response helps when you walk. The listing says it saves money because the battery is rechargeable and automatically charged.

Compared with the Infinity X1, it lacks the color options but provides both dusk sensing and motion sensing. It is a good fit for people who want a light that adapts to time of day. Test the brightness response before settling on a location. Unlike the GE 2 Pack, which holds a fixed 5 lumen glow, the Wennyn idles dim and rises as you walk by, which is the gentler behavior for a bedroom.
products.bestFor: Bedrooms and bathrooms that want a dim glow that brightens on movement.
pros: Dusk to dawn and motion sensing together
Dim glow at night, brighter on motion
cons: Single unit does not cover several rooms

products.name: ROSSEX 4 in 1 Emergency Lights, 3 Pack
products.description:
The ROSSEX 4 in 1 is the no-frills option. It plugs into a standard socket, charges its built-in lithium battery quickly, and switches on automatically in an outage. It also works as a standard flashlight, a night light and more, according to the listing.

The simplicity is its strength. There is no sensor setup to worry about and no color setting to pick. You plug it in, and it does its job. For households that want to cover three spots without learning anything new, it is a sensible set.

Compared with the GE 2 Pack, the ROSSEX provides a third unit in the pack. Compared with the Camelion, it lacks motion sensing. If you want straightforward backup in several rooms and are happy to leave the lights on a plain schedule, this is a dependable choice. Because it has few settings, it makes a good starter light for someone who has never owned an emergency light. The count matches the Camelion and Infinity X1 packs, but nothing here needs a sensor range or color temperature chosen before it works.
products.bestFor: Straightforward multi-room coverage without sensors to learn.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Night lights use a light sensor, a motion sensor, or both. The GE 2 Pack and Energizer 4 in 1 rely on dusk to dawn sensing, the Camelion and Infinity X1 use motion, and the Wennyn combines the two. A light sensor is predictable and glows steadily, while a motion sensor saves battery but may react to pets. Choose the sensor that matches how you move through the house. For a bedroom with a sleeping partner, the steady GE style is usually calmer than a light that blinks on every time someone turns over. For a long hallway, the Infinity X1 can start its glow before you reach the doorway.

A night light should be gentle. The GE lists a 5 lumen night mode, which is dim enough for a bedroom hallway. Higher levels can feel harsh at 3 in the morning. Prefer lights with a low default and a separate brighter mode for emergencies. The Wennyn idles in a dimmed state and rises only when you move, which is gentler on a light sleeper than a fixed glow.

In an outage you want enough light to see obstacles. The GE lists 40 lumens for the emergency and flashlight modes, which lights a room well enough to move around. Check the listing for emergency output, as not every light spells it out. Roughly 20 to 40 lumens is enough to navigate a hallway. If a listing does not publish emergency lumens, as with the Energizer and ROSSEX pages, plan for a handheld flashlight alongside it.

Warm light is easier on tired eyes than cool white. The Infinity X1 lets you choose 3000K warm, 4500K neutral or 6000K cool. Most other lights are fixed. If you wake at night often, a warm glow helps you fall back asleep. Try each color setting on the Infinity X1 on the first night and then leave it alone. Changing settings in the dark is not a task anyone enjoys.

Many of these lights lift out of the wall and become a flashlight, such as the Camelion, which folds out. Make sure the handle or fold-out design is easy to grip. A light you cannot hold comfortably is not much use as a flashlight. Try removing and reinserting it once to check. Practice lifting the light out of the wall once in daylight, so the grip and the release motion are familiar when it matters.

The rechargeable batteries in these lights lose capacity with age. The ROSSEX and Wennyn use built-in rechargeable batteries, and the Camelion promises no disposable cells. Test each light twice a year by pulling it from the wall. Replace any that fade quickly. A three-pack like the ROSSEX or Camelion gives you units to rotate, so one light can be tested at full drain while the others stay in place.

faq.q: What is a power failure night light?
faq.a: It is a plug-in night light with a built-in battery. It glows normally when power is on and switches to emergency mode when the power fails. Many lift out and serve as a flashlight. Think of it as a night light first and an emergency light second.

Night modes are dim, such as the GE at 5 lumens. Emergency modes are brighter, such as the GE at 40 lumens. Not every listing publishes numbers. Compare the listing on the product page before you buy so you know what is stated.

Light-sensing models glow from dusk to dawn, while motion models glow only when triggered. The battery matters only during an outage. Maker-stated runtimes vary. If the light is a motion model, expect shorter glow periods and longer battery life.

faq.q: Will a motion light wake me?
faq.a: A motion light only glows when something moves in front of it. Place it where it will not catch a sleeping partner. A light sensor model may be better for bedrooms. The Camelion and Infinity X1 are the motion models here, and the GE 2 Pack is the steadier choice for a shared room.

Pull the light from the wall and check that it stays lit for several minutes. Do this twice a year. Replace any that fade quickly. The GE's 40 lumen emergency mode makes the difference obvious, because a weak battery shows up as a visibly dim beam.
They work as small flashlights, but a dedicated flashlight is brighter. Keep both for flexibility. The Camelion folds out for easier handling. For long outages, a lantern or bulb is a better partner.
